title: The Diplomat Who Vanished Saving Thousands in Budapest #shorts
description:
In 1944, one Swedish diplomat bluffed the Nazis with a piece of paper — and saved tens of thousands of lives. Then he vanished.

Raoul Wallenberg was Sweden's special envoy in Budapest during the darkest months of World War II. He invented a protective passport called the Schutz-Pass — just paper stamped with Sweden's golden crowns. It was a bluff, but the Nazis and their Hungarian allies respected it. He climbed onto deportation trains and pulled people back from the edge of Auschwitz. He rented whole buildings, declared them Swedish soil, and sheltered thousands.

By winter, tens of thousands owed him their lives.

Then, in January 1945, the Soviets stormed into Budapest — and Wallenberg disappeared into their custody. He was never seen again. The man who faced down the Nazis was erased by the men who came after them.
